title: The Jacobian challenge (Christian Merten’s AG version), Part II
summary: Extend the field-level Jacobian challenge to smooth projective geometrically connected positive-genus curve families over noetherian bases. Build degree Picard torsors and the relative Jacobian, use the canonical principal polarization to obtain a section-free twice-theta bundle, establish actual-line-bundle descent and theta identities, and supply universal Faltings–Zhang constructions and the stable semi-abelian Hodge comparison.
readme: The definitive roadmap document is research/blueprint/readmes/JacobianChallengePartII.md. Generic Picard sheaves, rigidification, abelian schemes, duals, torsion and generalized Jacobians are imported from their owners. A global base point, degree-one line bundle or theta divisor is never part of the standing family hypotheses. Analytic metrics, adelic pairings and nondegeneracy are consumers rather than extra targets here. The reviewed packet specifies the signed Poincaré comparison and imports nodal duality and fibrewise ampleness from upstream StableReduction Layer2. Regeneration of the separately owned reader document must use these reviewed contracts.

stages.title: Relative Picard degree components
stages.description:
Unless narrowed explicitly, S is noetherian and π:X→S is smooth projective of relative dimension one, with geometrically connected fibres of constant genus g>0. Disconnected bases are handled componentwise. Picard objects are fppf sheaves; all equalities of bundles mean isomorphism classes unless a rigidification is specified.

Targets:

Relative degree components. For every d∈ℤ, Picᵈ_{X/S} is the sub-fppf-sheaf of the imported Pic_{X/S} whose geometric-fibre classes have degree d. A locally varying integer degree gives the disjoint union of these constant-degree pieces, not a single globally constant integer on disconnected T.

Local constancy of relative degree. For an invertible L on X_T, the function t↦deg(L_t)=χ(L_t)−χ(O_{X_t}) is locally constant on T and unchanged after any base extension of residue fields.

Relative curve Picard scheme. Pic_{X/S} is represented by a smooth separated S-group scheme, with open-and-closed quasi-projective pieces Picᵈ_{X/S} for d∈ℤ. Its degree-zero piece is the identity component. Representability commutes with arbitrary change of base.

Picard degree torsors. Tensoring by degree-zero classes makes Picᵈ_{X/S} an fppf torsor under Pic⁰_{X/S}; Picᵈ need not have an S-point. Its difference morphism Picᵈ×_S Picᵈ→Pic⁰ sends (L,M) to M⊗L⁻¹.

stages.title: Relative Jacobians and principal polarization
stages.description:
Unless narrowed explicitly, S is noetherian and π:X→S is smooth projective of relative dimension one, with geometrically connected fibres of constant genus g>0. Disconnected bases are handled componentwise. Picard objects are fppf sheaves; all equalities of bundles mean isomorphism classes unless a rigidification is specified.

Targets:

Relative Jacobian. J(X/S):=Pic⁰_{X/S}, with the tensor group law, is an abelian scheme of relative dimension g. No section of X/S is part of its data.

Properness of the relative Jacobian. For smooth projective geometrically connected X/S, Pic⁰_{X/S}→S is proper. Consequently it is projective locally over S and the canonical relatively ample twice-theta bundle of JC3 will make it projective over S.

Base change of the relative Jacobian. For every T→S, the Picard-sheaf base-change isomorphism restricts to a group-scheme isomorphism J(X/S)_T≅J(X_T/T), including infinitesimal base changes.

Canonical principal polarization. There is a canonical principal polarization λ_X:J→J∨, functorial in base change, defined without a global degree-one bundle on X. After an fppf cover with a degree-one bundle it agrees with the classical theta polarization, with Yuan’s Poincaré sign convention pinned in JC3.

stages.title: Section-free Abel and difference morphisms
stages.description:
Unless narrowed explicitly, S is noetherian and π:X→S is smooth projective of relative dimension one, with geometrically connected fibres of constant genus g>0. Disconnected bases are handled componentwise. Picard objects are fppf sheaves; all equalities of bundles mean isomorphism classes unless a rigidification is specified.

Targets:

Section-free Abel map. The diagonal relative effective Cartier divisor on X×_S X defines a canonical S-morphism a₁:X→Pic¹_{X/S}, taking a T-point x to O_{X_T}(Γ_x). It commutes with arbitrary base change and needs no section of π.

Degree-d Abel–Jacobi morphism. For an actual invertible α on X of constant relative degree d∈ℤ, i_α:X→J sends x to [O(dΓ_x)⊗α_T⁻¹]. The morphism exists for every d, including 0 and negative d.

Local pointed factorization. After any base change with a section x₀:X_T/T, i_α=t_β∘[d]∘i_{O(x₀)}, where β=[dO(x₀)−α_T]∈J(T). The equality holds as T-morphisms.

Degree-one Abel immersion. If d=1, i_α:X→J is a closed immersion over every noetherian S in the standing scope. No global section of X/S is required.

Finiteness of nonzero-degree Abel maps. For d≠0, i_α:X→J is finite over S. The statement allows negative d and characteristic dividing d. The degree-zero map is constant and is not finite on a nonempty curve fibre.

Curve difference morphism. j:X×_S X→J is δ∘(a₁,a₁), with j(x,y)=[O(Γ_y−Γ_x)]; it is defined without a section.

Difference as the Abel map over X. View X×_S X over the first X-factor. Its diagonal is a section and its Jacobian is X×_S J. The Abel map for O(Δ_X) is (x,y)↦(x,j(x,y)); forgetting the first coordinate gives j.

stages.title: Theta and normalized Poincaré identities
stages.description:
Unless narrowed explicitly, S is noetherian and π:X→S is smooth projective of relative dimension one, with geometrically connected fibres of constant genus g>0. Disconnected bases are handled componentwise. Picard objects are fppf sheaves; all equalities of bundles mean isomorphism classes unless a rigidification is specified.

Targets:

Normalized Jacobian Poincaré bundle. Let P_X on J×_S J be the pullback of the rigidified Poincaré bundle via the canonical identification of J with its dual, using Yuan’s convention: on a field fibre with theta line L, its class is m*L⁻¹⊗p₁*L⊗p₂*L. It is rigidified along both zero axes. The sign comparison between this convention and the supplier φ_L convention is a required named comparison.

Theta divisor with a degree-one class. Over a field K, for a smooth projective geometrically connected C of genus g>0 and an actual degree-one divisor α, θ_α is the image of Sym^{g−1}C→J, D↦[D−(g−1)α], with its effective Cartier divisor structure. For g=1 the symmetric power is Spec K and θ_α is the origin. This translates the parent theta construction to arbitrary degree-one α, which need not be effective or a rational point.

Canonical twice-theta bundle. Define Θ_X:=Δ_J*(P_X∨), an actual invertible sheaf on J with the induced zero rigidification. This is defined without a degree-one bundle on X; it is not a chosen theta divisor.

Pullback of inverse theta. i_α*O_J([-1]*θ_α)≅O_C(gα).

Pullback of theta. i_α*O_J(θ_α)≅ω_{C/K}⊗O_C((2−g)α).

Poincaré addition identity. In Pic(J×J), P=m*O_J(−θ_α)⊗p₁*O_J(θ_α)⊗p₂*O_J(θ_α). As a rigidified isomorphism, include the constant fibre normalization of O_J(θ_α) at the origin; the displayed formula alone is a class equality over the field.

Poincaré pullback on the curve square. In Pic(C×C), (i_α,i_α)*P=O(Δ_C)⊗p₁*O_C(−α)⊗p₂*O_C(−α). There is no assumption (2g−2)α=ω_C.

Theta doubling formula. [2]*O_J(θ_α)≅O_J(3θ_α+[-1]*θ_α) as a Picard class over K.

Poincaré diagonal identity. Δ_J*P≅O_J(−θ_α−[-1]*θ_α).

Geometric fibre twice-theta class. For every geometric point s of S, Θ_s is algebraically equivalent to twice a theta divisor on J_s. With a chosen degree-one α over the algebraically closed residue field, its Picard class is θ_α+[-1]*θ_α.

Symmetry of twice-theta. [-1]*Θ_X≅Θ_X as zero-rigidified bundles over S, not merely on geometric fibres.

Zero rigidification of twice-theta. The zero-axis trivializations of P induce e*Θ_X≅O_S, compatible with base change.

Relative ampleness of twice-theta. Θ_X is relatively ample for J→S; hence J→S is projective. The proof uses properness and the fibrewise ampleness criterion over noetherian S.

For the evaluation-normalized supplier bundle U with U_b=b and φ_L(a)=t_a*L⊗L⁻¹, define Yuan’s P_X by (id,−λ_X)*U. The signed comparison and fibre-at-zero rigidification are explicit. The proper-family fibrewise ampleness criterion is imported from upstream StableReduction Layer2.

stages.title: Actual Picard groups and descent
stages.description:
Unless narrowed explicitly, S is noetherian and π:X→S is smooth projective of relative dimension one, with geometrically connected fibres of constant genus g>0. Disconnected bases are handled componentwise. Picard objects are fppf sheaves; all equalities of bundles mean isomorphism classes unless a rigidification is specified.

Targets:

Actual fibrewise Picard subgroup. For a projective flat Y→S, Pic⁰(Y/S) is the subgroup of the actual Pic(Y) formed by line-bundle classes algebraically trivial on every geometric fibre. It is not Pic⁰_{Y/S}(S); comparison to that sheaf group requires a separate obstruction statement.

Picard subgroup along both projections. For projective flat Y₁,Y₂ over S, Pic⁰⁰(Y₁×_S Y₂) consists of actual line classes whose restrictions to every geometric fibre of each projection to Y₁ and to Y₂ are algebraically trivial.

Relative curve autoduality. There is a canonical base-change-compatible identification u:Pic⁰_{J/S}≅Pic⁰_{X/S} such that, for the actual degree-d α, i_α*= [d]∘u as morphisms of fppf group sheaves. The sign of u is characterized by degree-one Abel pullback.

Actual Picard classes and the Brauer obstruction. For proper flat Y/S with O_S≅f_*O_Y universally, 0→Pic(S)→Pic(Y)→Pic_{Y/S}(S)→Br(S)→Br(Y) is exact. For J/S its identity section kills the obstruction, so Pic⁰(J/S)/Pic(S)≅Pic⁰_{J/S}(S). For X/S the same map is only injective without a section.

Actual Picard pullback torsion cokernel. Let S be a normal integral quasi-projective scheme flat over ℤ or over a field, and let α have relative degree d>0. Every L∈Pic⁰(X/S) has a positive tensor power in the image of i_α*:Pic⁰(J/S)→Pic⁰(X/S). In particular the cokernel is a torsion group. No integral surjectivity is asserted.

Lift preserving both fibre conditions. In the arithmetic normal-base scope and for positive-degree i_α, every Pic⁰⁰ class on X×_S X has a positive power lifted through id_X×i_α to a class on X×_S J lying in Pic⁰⁰. The corresponding assertion through i_α×id_J lifts Pic⁰⁰(X×J) to Pic⁰⁰(J×J).

Bi-Picard pullback torsion cokernel. Under the same S, X, α and d>0 hypotheses, (i_α,i_α)*:Pic⁰⁰(J×_S J)→Pic⁰⁰(X×_S X) has torsion cokernel.

Axis-normalized Picard subgroup. Over a field K, with a rational x₀∈C(K), Pic⁻(C²) is the subgroup of actual Pic(C²) whose restrictions to C×{x₀} and {x₀}×C are trivial; Pic⁻(J²) uses the two zero axes. These are classes with trivial restrictions, not chosen rigidifications and not the larger Pic⁰⁰ subgroup.

Pointed square Picard comparison. With x₀ as above and i=i_{O(x₀)}, (i,i)*:Pic⁻(J²)→Pic⁻(C²) is an isomorphism. The application over complete nonarchimedean K uses only this algebraic assertion here; its metrics belong to the Arakelov owner.

stages.title: Faltings–Zhang and canonical shifts
stages.description:
Unless narrowed explicitly, S is noetherian and π:X→S is smooth projective of relative dimension one, with geometrically connected fibres of constant genus g>0. Disconnected bases are handled componentwise. Picard objects are fppf sheaves; all equalities of bundles mean isomorphism classes unless a rigidification is specified.

Targets:

Canonical-bundle Abel morphism. For g>1, ω_{X/S} has relative degree 2g−2, so i_ω(x)=[(2g−2)Γ_x−ω_{X/S}] is a finite S-morphism X→J.

Universal shifted canonical morphism. For g>1, τ:J×_S X→J×_S J is (y,x)↦(y,y+i_ω(x)); it is a morphism over the first J-factor and has no global-section hypothesis.

Faltings–Zhang morphism. For m≥1, FZ_m:X^{m+1}_S→J^m_S sends (x₀,…,x_m) to (j(x₀,x₁),…,j(x₀,x_m)). It is defined without a section and without a maximal-variation hypothesis.

Shifted Faltings–Zhang morphism. For g>1 and m≥1, τ_m:X^m_S×_S J→J^m_S sends (x₁,…,x_m,y) to (i_ω(x₁)+y,j(x₁,x₂),…,j(x₁,x_m)). The source order, first shift and unscaled remaining differences are part of the definition.

Triangular change on represented points. For any scheme S, any group object A of Over(S), any T∈Over(S), and n≥0, there is a natural equivalence of (n+1)-tuples of T-valued points of A: R(q)₀=q₀, R(q)_r=q_r q₀⁻¹ for r≠0. Its inverse sends r to (r₀,r₁r₀,…,r_nr₀). Multiplicative notation is Mathlib’s notation for group objects; on the Jacobian it means subtraction and addition. The construction uses actual morphisms T→A, not an abstract point-set replacement for A.

Shifted-power factorization. Let B_m(x₁,…,x_m,y)=(i_ω(x₁)+y,…,i_ω(x_m)+y). After the triangular change R on J^m, R∘B_m=D∘τ_m, where D fixes the first coordinate and multiplies each tail by 2g−2. This equality holds as S-morphisms; D is a finite locally free isogeny for g>1.

stages.title: Stable curve–Jacobian Hodge comparison
stages.description:
Unless narrowed explicitly, S is noetherian and π:X→S is smooth projective of relative dimension one, with geometrically connected fibres of constant genus g>0. Disconnected bases are handled componentwise. Picard objects are fppf sheaves; all equalities of bundles mean isomorphism classes unless a rigidification is specified.

Targets:

Picard Lie algebra and coherent cohomology. For an integral noetherian S and a stable connected nodal genus-g>1 family π:X→S, let G=Pic⁰_{X/S} be the smooth separated semi-abelian group supplied by Néron R11.4. There is a canonical O_S-linear isomorphism Lie(G/S)≅R¹π_*O_X, compatible with base change.

Curve and Jacobian Hodge bundles. Under the hypotheses of the Picard Lie comparison, relative duality gives π_*ω_{X/S}≅e*Ω¹_{G/S}. Both are locally free of rank g and commute with the allowed base changes; the right side uses invariant differentials of the semi-abelian G.

Curve–Jacobian Hodge line isomorphism. For the same stable family, λ_X:=det(π_*ω_{X/S}) is canonically isomorphic to det(e*Ω¹_{G/S}); the isomorphism is the determinant of the vector-bundle comparison and is compatible with its base-change isomorphisms.

The nodal relative dualizing sheaf, genus-rank cohomology and relative-duality/base-change maps are supplied by upstream StableReduction Layer2; the field-only parent Jacobian duality is not used as a stable-family theorem.

stages.title: Universal curves with full level
stages.description:
Unless narrowed explicitly, S is noetherian and π:X→S is smooth projective of relative dimension one, with geometrically connected fibres of constant genus g>0. Disconnected bases are handled componentwise. Picard objects are fppf sheaves; all equalities of bundles mean isomorphism classes unless a rigidification is specified.

Targets:

Universal Jacobian with full level. Fix g≥2, ℓ≥3 invertible on the base, and the same pairing component and cyclotomic convention as the imported fine-level curve scheme. Apply JC0–JC3 to its smooth projective universal curve: obtain Pic=⨆_d Picᵈ, the principally polarized J, its induced full symplectic level-ℓ structure, and the section-free C→Pic¹ morphism.

Faltings–Zhang for the universal curve. For every S→M_g[ℓ] in the chosen level convention and m≥1, base change the universal curve and its Jacobian. FZ_m:C_S^{m+1}→J_S^m is a morphism over S. On a field fibre with P₀∈C(k), fixing its first coordinate gives the m-fold pointed Abel embedding C−P₀.
